reference_fields: OSU EC 1617 Blackberry Cultivars for Oregon
Oregon State University Extension cultivar guide for trailing, erect, semierect, primocane-fruiting erect, and blackberry/red raspberry hybrid blackberries grown in Oregon

locations.name: Oregon State University Extension Service, Corvallis, Oregon

categories.name: Trailing blackberries for Oregon
categories.description: OSU EC 1617 lists these trailing blackberry cultivars in approximate order of ripening for Oregon

categories.name: Blackberry/red raspberry hybrids for Oregon
categories.description: OSU EC 1617 lists these blackberry/red raspberry hybrid cultivars in approximate order of ripening and says they are technically blackberries

categories.name: Erect blackberries for Oregon
categories.description: OSU EC 1617 lists these erect blackberry cultivars in approximate order of ripening for Oregon

categories.name: Primocane-fruiting erect blackberries for Oregon
categories.description: OSU EC 1617 lists these primocane-fruiting erect blackberry cultivars in approximate order of ripening for Oregon

categories.name: Semierect blackberries for Oregon
categories.description: OSU EC 1617 lists these semierect blackberry cultivars in approximate order of ripening for Oregon

rows.name: Obsidian
rows.fruit: Large size, good firmness, black, fair shape, excellent flavor, very early ripening
rows.harvest_time: very early; harvest typically starts in the third week of June in Oregon's Willamette Valley

rows.name: Metolius
rows.fruit: Medium size, firm, black, excellent uniform shape, excellent flavor, very early ripening

rows.name: Silvan
rows.fruit: Large size, soft, dark purple, fair shape, excellent flavor
rows.comment: Very soft and does not hold up in heat

rows.name: Cascade
rows.fruit: Small to medium size, soft, purple, excellent flavor, early ripening
rows.comment: Not productive enough

rows.name: Olallie
rows.fruit: Medium size, soft, black, lumpy shape, excellent flavor, early ripening
rows.comment: Was grown commonly in California for U-pick and fresh sales, but in Oregon it is lower yielding and more sensitive to winter cold injury than Marion

rows.name: Black Diamond
rows.fruit: Large size, firm, black, very uniform shape, good flavor

rows.name: Columbia Star
rows.fruit: Large size, firm, very uniform shape, outstanding flavor and processing quality
rows.comment: Too new for the 2014 PDF table to fully evaluate but very promising; source table names this as Columbia Star (U.S. Plant Patent pending)

rows.name: Kotata
rows.fruit: Small to medium size, good firmness, dark purple, uniform shape, excellent flavor
rows.comment: May be difficult to market processed but popular for fresh market

rows.name: Marion
rows.fruit: Medium size, soft, dark purple, uneven shape, excellent flavor
rows.comment: Source table notes this is often called marionberry

rows.name: Wild Treasure
rows.plant: Thornless, very vigorous. Thin canes break easily, so commercial growers should use alternate-year production systems or train canes very gently to avoid breakage
rows.fruit: Small size, medium firmness, dark purple, very uniform shape, excellent flavor
rows.yield: Low to high, depending on amount of damage during cane training

rows.name: Onyx
rows.plant: Vigorous, thorny, fairly upright growth habit for a trailing blackberry
rows.fruit: Medium size, uniform shape, firm, black, excellent sweet, mild flavor
rows.comment: Too new for the 2014 PDF table to fully evaluate but expected to do well in fresh market; source table names this as Onyx (U.S. Plant Patent 22,358)

rows.name: Thornless Evergreen
rows.fruit: Small size, soft, black, mild but good flavor, August-September ripening season, prone to gray mold after fall rains
rows.comment: Nursery plants not available; source describes this as a thornless chimera and combines it in one table row with Everthornless

rows.name: Everthornless
rows.fruit: Small size, soft, black, mild but good flavor, August-September ripening season, prone to gray mold after fall rains
rows.comment: Nursery plants not available; source describes this as a genetically thornless clone and combines it in one table row with Thornless Evergreen

rows.name: Logan
rows.plant: Moderate vigor, thorny, canes susceptible to disease. Thornless Logan is available, but it is not genetically thornless and will produce thorny canes
rows.fruit: Medium size, more like raspberry than blackberry in color and flavor, deep red color, conic shape, excellent firmness but tender skin, excellent but distinctive flavor, hard to pick
rows.comment: Source table notes this is often called loganberry

rows.name: Tayberry
rows.fruit: Medium size, glossy, reddish purple, good firmness but tender skin, excellent but unique tart flavor, very hard to pick, fruit damaged easily by hot weather
rows.comment: Successful niche markets have been developed, but low yield and difficulty of harvest make this nearly impossible to produce economically

rows.name: Newberry
rows.fruit: Large size, blocky, glossy, reddish purple to dark purple, firmer and tougher skin than Boysen, excellent flavor, but despite Boysen look, does not have Boysen flavor
rows.comment: Too new for the 2014 PDF table to fully evaluate

rows.name: Thornless Boysen
rows.fruit: Small to medium size, lumpy, purple, fair flavor
rows.comment: Source says this thornless cultivar is the color of Boysen but was developed in California and does not have the flavor of the original Boysen

rows.name: Boysen
rows.fruit: Large size, soft, lumpy, purple, unique and very good flavor
rows.comment: Source table notes this is often called boysenberry; source also says Nectarberry and Youngberry are very similar to Boysen

rows.name: Natchez
rows.fruit: Large to very large size, very firm, black, glossy, picks easily, seedy, fair flavor. Can have variable fruit set with lumpy fruit
rows.yield: Medium; yield can vary from year to year because of biennial bearing
rows.comment: Source table names this as Natchez (U.S. Plant Patent 20,891)

rows.name: Ouachita
rows.fruit: Medium size, firm, tough skin, attractive, black, glossy, round, prone to sunburn or UV damage, fair flavor
rows.yield: Medium; yield can vary from year to year because of biennial bearing
rows.comment: Uneven performance in commercial fields; source table names this as Ouachita (U.S. Plant Patent 17,162)

rows.name: Osage
rows.fruit: Small to medium size, firm, tough skin, black, glossy, round, fair flavor
rows.comment: Too new for the 2014 PDF table to fully evaluate; source table names this as Osage (U.S. Plant Patent pending)

rows.name: Apache
rows.fruit: Large size, firm, tough skin, black, glossy, round, lumpy, seedy, prone to sunburn or UV damage, fair flavor
rows.comment: Source table names this as Apache (U.S. Plant Patent 11,865)

rows.name: Illini Hardy
rows.fruit: Medium to large size, soft, black, glossy, tends to be bitter
rows.comment: An option when too cold to grow most blackberries

rows.name: Navaho
rows.fruit: Small to medium size, firm, tough skin, attractive, black, glossy, round, good flavor, ships well

rows.name: Prime-Jim
rows.fruit: Large size, soft to medium-firm, moderately tender skin, black, glossy, seedy, fair flavor, season is from late August to first frost
rows.comment: Source table combines Prime-Jim and Prime-Jan in one cultivar entry and lists U.S. Plant Patent 16,989

rows.name: Prime-Jan
rows.fruit: Large size, soft to medium-firm, moderately tender skin, black, glossy, seedy, fair flavor, season is from late August to first frost
rows.comment: Source table combines Prime-Jim and Prime-Jan in one cultivar entry and lists U.S. Plant Patent 15,788

rows.name: Prime-Ark 45
rows.plant: Moderately vigorous to vigorous, very thorny
rows.fruit: Large to very large size, firm, moderately tender skin, black, glossy, seedy, good flavor, season is from early September to first frost
rows.comment: Limited yield in short season; source table names this as Prime-Ark 45 (U.S. Plant Patent 22,449)

rows.name: Prime-Ark Freedom
rows.fruit: Small to medium, moderately firm, black, glossy, seedy, season is from early September to first frost
rows.yield: Low unless grown in a tunnel
rows.comment: Too new for the 2014 PDF table to fully evaluate; source table lists U.S. Plant Patent pending

rows.name: Loch Ness
rows.fruit: Medium size, fair firmness, attractive, black, glossy, oblong, prone to sunburn or UV damage, fair flavor

rows.name: Hull Thornless
rows.fruit: Medium size, fair firmness, black, glossy, round, prone to sunburn or UV damage, fair flavor
rows.comment: Too soft to ship well

rows.name: Triple Crown
rows.fruit: Medium to large size, fair firmness, attractive, black, glossy, round, lumpy, prone to sunburn or UV damage, berries can ripen unevenly, good flavor
rows.comment: Limited shelf life

rows.name: Doyle's Thornless
rows.fruit: Small to medium size, fair firmness, black, glossy, round, lumpy, noticeably large seeds, poor to fair flavor

rows.name: Black Satin
rows.fruit: Small to medium size, soft, attractive, black, glossy, round, prone to sunburn or UV damage, fair flavor

rows.name: Chester Thornless
rows.fruit: Small to medium size, firm, tough skin, attractive, black, glossy, round, prone to sunburn or UV damage, fair flavor, susceptible to red berry mite
rows.comment: Ships fresh very well
